devices.title: Converters & Interfaces
devices.approximate: * Approximate. This interface uses plain CoreAudio rather than ASIO, so Port Setup has no real channel numbers for it. The numbering is a best guess (sequential per device), not confirmed Cubase data.
devices.conflictsHeading: Channel conflicts: these channels already belong to another device in the same direction.
devices.couldNotRead: Couldn't read that file as a converter/interface export.
devices.deleteDetail: This only removes it from StudioPatchbay. Nothing changes in Cubase.
devices.detectedPortsHelp: From Port Setup, for reference while entering channel numbers.
devices.discardDetail: You'll lose the changes you made here.
devices.emptyHelp: Add the converters and interfaces in your studio, or import a setup someone has shared with you.
devices.helpType: Converter: a box like a Ferrofish or ADI-648 between the interface's digital port and external gear, with no connection to the computer. Audio Interface: a self-contained USB/Thunderbolt device with its own analog I/O.
devices.helpConnector: The digital protocol this device uses to connect to the audio interface, not what is on its other side. Only categorisation and colour; it does not change the channel numbers.
devices.helpDirections: Most devices have both. Choose output or input only for hardware that is one-way, such as a monitor system without an input path.
devices.helpChannels: OUT and IN usually start at the same channel; they differ only when Cubase numbers this connector's two sides differently. Only starts that overlap no other device are offered.
devices.importAddBlocked: %COUNT% have a channel conflict with your devices or each other, so "Add to Current" is off.
devices.importReplaceBlocked: %COUNT% conflict with each other within this file, so "Replace All" is off.
devices.importMismatch: %COUNT% of %TOTAL% match no port detected here; they were probably made for other hardware.
devices.importNoPorts: No ports detected here, so the hardware check is skipped. Open a Cubase project with your interface and reload for a meaningful check.
devices.importEmpty: That file doesn't contain any converters or interfaces.
devices.importNoPort: %DIR% ch %RANGE%: no matching port detected here
devices.interfaceNamesHelp: Optional: the hardware each port is on, e.g. "RME HDSPe MADI FX".
devices.noPorts: No ports detected. Open a Cubase project with this interface active, then reload.
devices.removeAllDetail: This clears the whole list and can't be undone. Consider exporting a backup first.
